section: Educational Psychology · Ch5 — Kohlberg: All 6 Stages
subject: Educational Psychology
stem: A child says, 'I'll share my toy with my friend only if he shares his toy with me too.' This 'what's-in-it-for-me' reasoning reflects Kohlberg's:
explanation: Stage 2 reasoning is transactional — right action serves one's own interests, with fairness understood as an equal exchange ('you scratch my back, I'll scratch yours') — distinct from Stage 1's pure punishment-avoidance.

section: Educational Psychology · Ch5 — Kohlberg: All 6 Stages
subject: Educational Psychology
stem: A teenager decides not to cheat on a test, thinking 'a good student wouldn't do that, and my parents and teachers would be disappointed in me.' This reasoning, focused on being seen as a 'good person' by others, reflects Kohlberg's:

options.option_text: Stage 3 — Interpersonal Accord and Conformity ('good boy/girl' orientation)

explanation: Stage 3 reasoning seeks approval and conformity to social/interpersonal expectations — living up to what 'good people' (family, peers) expect — the first conventional-level stage.

section: Educational Psychology · Ch5 — Kohlberg: All 6 Stages
subject: Educational Psychology
stem: Kohlberg's six stages are grouped into three levels. Which is the correct grouping?

options.option_text: All six stages belong to a single level with no grouping

explanation: Pre-conventional (Stages 1-2: punishment-obedience, individualism-exchange), Conventional (Stages 3-4: interpersonal accord, law-and-order), Post-conventional (Stages 5-6: social contract, universal ethical principles) — the standard three-level, six-stage structure.
